items.q: The normal magnesium interval printed here is ___ mEq/L.
items.exp: The chapter uses 1.5–2 mEq/L; units must be checked before comparing numerical values. (Book p892)

items.q: A magnesium result of 1 mmol/L is equivalent to which pair?
items.exp: Divalent magnesium gives 2 mEq per mmol, and its molar mass gives approximately 2.4 mg/dL per mmol/L. (Book p892)

items.q: Magnesium is the ___ most abundant intracellular cation, after ___.
items.exp: The source ranks intracellular potassium first and magnesium second. (Book p892)

items.q: Match the following magnesium absorption entries — 1) Principal intestinal site 2) Net dietary absorption 3) Paracellular share … A) 80–90% B) Ileum C) 30%
items.exp: The chapter assigns the ileum, 30% net absorption and 80–90% paracellular transport. (Book p892)

items.q: Which is the odd one out in the page's ileal-absorption association?
opts: Calcium as the principal jejunal mineral
items.exp: The source groups magnesium with ileal B12 and bile-acid absorption, while its calcium comparison emphasizes the jejunum. (Book p892)

items.q: The channels named for transcellular intestinal magnesium uptake are ___ and ___.
items.exp: The source identifies TRPM6/7 for magnesium, unlike TRPV channels used in calcium transport. (Book p892)

items.q: A patient with an inherited thiazide-like salt-wasting phenotype develops hypomagnesemia. Which defect fits the source link?
items.exp: Gitelman syndrome involves the DCT Na–Cl cotransporter, and thiazides can produce a related magnesium-wasting phenotype. (Book p892)

items.q: Match the following renal magnesium shares — 1) TAL 2) PCT 3) DCT … A) 65% B) 25% C) 10%
items.exp: The table gives TAL 65%, PCT 25% and DCT 10%; do not confuse this order with calcium handling. (Book p892)

items.q: Assess renal magnesium transport: I TAL and PCT uptake are described as active/transcellular. II DCT uptake is described as active/transcellular.
items.exp: These route distinctions explain why the DCT uses regulated magnesium channels while bulk TAL transport follows the paracellular pathway. (Book p892)

items.q: A patient receiving cetuximab develops magnesium wasting. Which pathway is most directly implicated?
opts: Vitamin D activation of TAL ROMK
items.exp: EGF regulates TRPM6 in the DCT; EGFR blockade by cetuximab interferes with magnesium conservation. (Book p892)

items.q: The TAL paracellular proteins carrying calcium and magnesium are claudin ___ and ___.
items.exp: The schematic names claudin-16/19; defects can impair renal divalent-cation handling. (Book p892)

items.q: Blood calcium rises and activates the TAL calcium-sensing receptor. What direction of calcium reabsorption is shown?
opts: Unchanged reabsorption at every calcium level
items.exp: The diagram shows high blood calcium activating CaSR, which inhibits calcium reabsorption; TAL salt transport supplies the driving force for paracellular Ca/Mg handling. (Book p892)

items.q: Match the following TAL diagram components — 1) NKCC2 2) ROMK 3) ClC-Kb/Barttin … A) Potassium recycling B) Basolateral chloride exit machinery C) Na–K–2Cl entry
items.exp: NKCC2 and ROMK support the lumen-positive driving force; ClC-Kb and its Barttin partner provide basolateral chloride handling in the figure. (Book p892)

items.q: For Bartter type 1, assess: I The source highlights hypercalciuria. II Its written hypomagnesuria label is a reliable description of a magnesium-wasting mechanism.
items.exp: The note associates type 1 with hypercalciuria and gives a 20% frequency for a magnesium abnormality, but writes hypomagnesuria. That word means low urinary magnesium and conflicts with magnesium wasting; do not silently equate it with hypomagnesemia. (Book p892)

items.q: Match the following DCT diagram labels to roles — 1) EGFR 2) Na/K-ATPase 3) TRPM6/7 … A) Apical magnesium entry B) Basolateral sodium/potassium gradient C) EGF signaling receptor
items.exp: These labeled components connect growth-factor signaling and basolateral ion gradients to magnesium entry through TRPM channels. (Book p892)

items.q: The DCT figure labels SLC41A1 or CNNM2 near the basolateral ___ pathway.
items.exp: The figure places these magnesium-handling proteins at the basolateral side, not at the apical TRPM entry site. (Book p892)

items.q: Assess the DCT illustration: I Kir4.1/Kir5.1 are shown as basolateral potassium-channel partners. II HNF1B/PCBD1 are presented as regulatory labels, not luminal magnesium pores.
items.exp: The diagram separates basolateral potassium handling and regulatory factors from TRPM-mediated apical magnesium entry. (Book p892)
